node.title: Processing an encoded file backwards
node.author: LanX
node.doctext:
Hi

lets say I wanted a sliding window to search a file from end to start.²

Could do this with [DOC://seek|seek] and [DOC://read|read] in a loop.

Now is seek operating on byte boundaries ,but read depends on the encryption layer. °

What's the best way than to read an encoded file, like in UTF-8, backwards ?

Is read fail-proof when accidentally starting inside a wide character after a seek?

Or is it better to open :raw and to search the next character (or line) boundary manually and to decode with [DOC://Encode|Encode] then?

I'm aware of [METAMOD://File::ReadBackwards] , but want to understand the mechanisms better and operate on windows and not lines.

Cheers Rolf
(addicted to the Perl Programming Language :)
[id://1153804|Wikisyntax for the Monastery] FootballPerl is like chess, only without the dice

updates
°) DB<1> open $fh,'<','input2' DB<2> read $fh => $in, 100 DB<3> p tell $fh 114 # surprise DB<4> open $fh,'<:raw','input2' DB<5> p tell $fh 0 DB<6> read $fh => $in, 100 DB<7> p tell $fh 100 DB<8>

²) I've been asked what I mean with "sliding window", please see this [id://875767|sliding window] description. There I start from the beginning, but it's often favorable to start from the end. ([choroba]++ for pm'ing me)
